findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Due to this violation being a third repeat violation, this violation is now on compliance conference. A follow up is scheduled on 4/3/2026 to ensure that all employees who are not CFPMs have obtained their food handler certificate, or according to Colleen Kelley, the Director of Environmental Health, the permit for the facility will be suspended. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

The facility is currently using ice to hold the food that requires temperature control for safety. The pickles usually held in this table are labeled perishable.  The ice for holding food was to be a temporary solution after the original violation cited on 5/8/24. The violation shall be corrected by the follow up date listed (6/26/24)

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the ice machine bin lid to be broken and not functioning properly. Repair the lid as soon as possible to protect food from potential contamination. Department expects that this repair shall be made in 10 days. A follow up inspection will take place. 

3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 - (REPEAT) Inspector observed several priority/priority foundation violations during the inspection. Foods were ordered to be discarded during today’s inspection due to multiple coolers not being operable.  Because of the risk of foodborne illness due to the practices observed and the presence of priority/priority foundation violations, a 30-day follow-up is being issued to ensure that all priority/priority foundation violations remain corrected. A follow-up will occur on June 10 to insure correction of all Priority and Priority foundation items and to insure maintenance to facility and equipment.
Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Despite having multiple employees present in the facility, no one was observed washing hands. There were multiple times staff was observed moving between tasks and donning and doffing gloves but no hand washing occurred. See that education occurs to employees on proper hand washing. Manager and operations were walking through the facility with inspectors so hand washing was not immediately being addressed. See that staff is properly educated on hand washing techniques. Will revisit hand washing on the June 10 inspection. 
 (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11:  Observed employee using a cup as a scoop in the drive thru. Discussed with employee and a proper scoop was used. 
Also, observed ice scoop with handle stored within ice in the ice machine basin by the back door. Ice scoop was properly stored during the inspection. 
(D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed gross food debris and paper toweling pieces to be within the hand washing basin of the frontline hand sink. Removed during the inspection. The hand sink should not be used for anything but hand washing. 
(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Observed two rusted shelves atop a preparation sink (by the back door) on which chicken is held. This is a potential for cross contamination. The shelves should be pulled from use. Stop using rusted shelving for food storage. 
 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.12: A number of surfaces are missing routine cleaning. See that the soda service station at the drive-thru is receiving detail cleaning. The interior of the preparation cooler (serious soil accumulation along the base and top), the interior of the upright freezer (serious accumulation of fry crumbs and food debris), the bun toaster (crumbs and soil), and the re-thermalizer (thickly coated with food). Clean food contact surfaces so there is no potential for cross contamination.  
(A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: The re-thermalizer is observed holding foods at 162F. The food should be reheated at 165F. Popeye’s policy is to reheat the foods to 180F within the unit. The facility reset the unit to 180F and the food quickly gained temp to 172F. Cease setting the reheat temperature to anything less than 165F. 
 (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The upright hot holding unit between the preparation cooler and the upright freezer is not working. Remove this unit or insure it is in working order. 
(A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16:  Observed a number of coolers to not be working within the facility: the preparation cooler is holding mayonnaise at 49 (unit at 67) and the upright freezer adjacent to the preparation cooler is holding temperature at 56F. A number of foods were discarded from these two cold-holding units. Operations manager was present and discarding items as we were moving through the facility. Ice was placed at the basin of the prep cooler to support the use of the mayos and pickles within the prep cooler. Cease use of the non-functioning units until the are serviced. 
(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: There are a number of drain flies and fruit flies around the mop sink. Inspector tapped the chemical dispenser and at least a dozen flew from the unit. Several more were observed around the walls. See that the facility walls, floor, and ceiling are scrubbed and maintained so they are free of pests. Drain flies are incredibly hard to remove. Contact pest control and clean so you are working in unison to actively remove the pests. 

PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-301.12: The triple sink has wash and sanitize basins that are not capable of properly holding and draining water. Repair or replace the sinks so they properly operate. 
(A) Sink with 3-compartments shall be provided for EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. (B) Sinks shall be capable of accommodating the immersion of the largest piece of EQUIPMENT or UTENSIL. (C) Sinks shall be capable of properly draining and containing water according to LAW (Pf).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Overall, the facility would benefit from a deep cleaning. Pay particular attention to: 1) plumbing coming from the dish machine (black with soil); 2) floor drain covers (black with soil throughout facility); 3) interior of coolers (food crumbs); 4) ceilings over fryers (dust); 5) ceiling in walk-in cooler (coated with mold); 6) dust on the fans of the upright cooler. Clean the aforementioned surfaces. SCDPH will return within thirty days to check on cleaning progress within this facility. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: Observed floor tiles to be missing from in-front of the fryers. Repair the missing floor tiles. 
The wall to the right of the ice machine has several holes present. Seal the holes. 
(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Physical facilities should be in good repair.
